newsitem.title: USA: Harcourt General's profits slip due to seasonal loss.
newsitem.headline: Harcourt General's profits slip due to seasonal loss.

text.p: Harcourt General Inc. said Thursday that its profits plunged more than 70 percent in its fiscal second quarter as seasonal losses at its publishing unit more than doubled.

The textbook publisher and speciality retailer said net income for the three months ended April 30 fell to $3.1 million, or 4 cents a share, from $10.4 million, or 14 cents a share. Revenues grew to $880 million from $844 million.

The company, which is based in Chestnut Hill, Mass., said that while its publishing revenues edged up to $188 million from $185.6 million, its seasonal operating loss jumped to $33 million from $14.9 million.

"As expected, this operating loss includes approximately $8 million of incremental plate amortization expenses in the current quarter for new instructional programmes as well as increased marketing and selling expenses to pursue the large number of significant school textbook adoption opportunities that are taking place this year," Chairman Richard A. Smith said in a statement.

Harcourt General, which publishes elementary and high school textbooks, typically has operating losses in its first two fiscal quarters, when major selling and marketing expenses are incurred. Most sales take place later in the year.

Harcourt on May 13 reached a friendly agreement to buy National Education Corp. for about $800 million. The deal broke up a stock merger between National Education and Sylvan Learnings Systems Inc. that had eroded in value since it was announced in March.

The company said operating earnings from its speciality retailing segment -- which includes the Neiman Marcus and Bergdorf Goodman retail chains -- increased to $54.3 million from $48.6 million a year ago, reflecting improved performances by the two upscale store chains.
Harcourt General's stock slipped 12.5 cents to $45.75 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
